issues.description: Syntax error: Missing closing backtick on line 78. The template literal is not properly closed, which will cause compilation failure.
issues.suggestion: Close the backtick: Change the last line from 'const row = rows[0]`;' to 'const row = rows[0];'

issues.description: PCI DSS Violation: Full credit card numbers are being processed and potentially stored in plaintext. The chargeCard function extracts card data, but the original payment object containing full card number is passed through the application, violating PCI compliance requirements.
issues.suggestion: Never store or log full card numbers. Use tokenization with a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, Square, Braintree). Pass only a token instead of PaymentDetails containing full card numbers.

issues.description: Weak card validation: Card number validation only checks length (16 chars) but doesn't perform Luhn algorithm checksum validation. This allows invalid card numbers to pass validation.
issues.suggestion: Implement Luhn algorithm validation: Validate the card number checksum before processing payment.

issues.description: Insecure logging in error handling (line 70): console.error() logs the full error object which may contain sensitive payment data or stack traces that could expose system details.
issues.suggestion: Replace sensitive error logging with sanitized messages. Use structured logging with sanitization in production. Never log full error objects containing financial data.

issues.description: Date validation bug: The expiry date parsing assumes 2-digit year format (2000 + year) but doesn't properly handle the century boundary. This creates dates in 2000-2025 but breaks for years 50-99 and beyond.
issues.suggestion: Use a proper date library (date-fns, moment) or implement proper century logic based on current date.

issues.description: Off-by-one error in expiry validation: The expiry check doesn't account for the last day of the expiry month. Cards valid through a month may be rejected prematurely.
issues.suggestion: Adjust the expiry check to consider the last day of the expiry month: const expiryEnd = new Date(fullYear, parseInt(month), 0, 23, 59, 59).

issues.description: Hard-coded pricing values embedded in the function. Pricing should be externalized to configuration or database for easier updates without code changes.
issues.suggestion: Move pricing to a configuration file or database table: const SUBSCRIPTION_CONFIG = { pricing: { premium: 9.99, enterprise: 49.99 } }.

issues.description: Insufficient input validation: payment.amount is accepted as-is from user input without validation. A user could submit negative amounts or extremely large values.
issues.suggestion: Add validation in validatePaymentDetails: if (payment.amount <= 0 || payment.amount > 100000) return false;

issues.description: Database architecture stores sensitive payment data (card_last_four). Even partial card data should be minimal and separately encrypted.
issues.suggestion: Consider using a payment token instead of storing any card data. If last_four must be stored, ensure the payment table is separately encrypted and access-controlled.

issues.description: Type safety issue: No runtime validation that userId is a valid user. No checks for null/undefined userId.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: if (!userId || typeof userId !== 'string') throw new Error('Invalid userId').

issues.description: Missing error handling in getUserSubscription: If JSON.parse(row.features) fails due to corrupted data, the function will crash without proper error handling.
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch: try { features: JSON.parse(row.features) } catch (error) { throw new Error('Corrupted subscription data'); }

issues.description: Missing error handling in hasFeatureAccess: If JSON.parse(subscription.features) fails, the function will throw an unhandled error instead of gracefully handling corrupted data.
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch block with proper error recovery.

issues.description: Generic error handling: The catch block doesn't distinguish between different failure types (network error, validation error, database error). All failures return false without context.
issues.suggestion: Distinguish error types and provide better error context for debugging and monitoring.

issues.description: Missing null/undefined check: The function doesn't validate that the database query returns rows with expected structure before accessing row.user_id, row.tier, etc.
issues.suggestion: Validate row structure: if (!row.user_id || !row.tier) { throw new Error('Invalid subscription record'); }

issues.description: Regex escape character inconsistency: The expiryRegex uses unnecessary escape characters that make the pattern harder to read.
issues.suggestion: Simplify the regex pattern for clarity and consistency.

codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL ISSUES FOUND: This code has multiple serious security and correctness problems that must be addressed before production use. The most critical issue is handling raw credit card data which violates PCI DSS compliance (use tokenization instead). There is also a syntax error that prevents compilation. Card validation lacks Luhn algorithm checks, error logging exposes sensitive data, and date calculations have edge cases. Missing error handling for JSON parsing could cause crashes. The lack of test coverage combined with these issues makes this code high-risk for financial operations.

testCoverage.summary: The src/premium.ts file contains critical payment processing and subscription management logic with zero test coverage. All six functions are completely untested, exposing significant risks in security-sensitive areas (card validation, payment processing), business logic (pricing, feature access), and data integrity (database operations, subscription state). The most critical gaps are in processPremiumPayment() and validatePaymentDetails(), which handle financial transactions and sensitive card data. Recommended immediate action: Create comprehensive test suite covering validation edge cases, success/failure payment paths, database error handling, and integration flows.

refactorings.summary: src/premium.ts contains solid business logic but needs refactoring in several key areas for production readiness. The highest-impact improvements are: (1) extracting database queries into a Repository pattern for centralized data access, (2) extracting validation logic into focused, testable functions, (3) moving configuration to module-level objects, and (4) extracting shared subscription retrieval logic. These changes will significantly improve testability (currently 0% coverage), maintainability, and extensibility. The code follows basic structure but lacks separation of concerns. Additional modernizations include better error handling, explicit type annotations, and simplified conditional logic.

recommendations.description: Remove raw credit card handling and implement tokenization. The current implementation processes and stores full card numbers, violating PCI DSS requirements. Replace with a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, Square, Braintree) that handles tokenization.
Fix syntax error on line 78. Missing closing backtick in template literal prevents code compilation: 'const row = rows[0]`;' should be 'const row = rows[0];'
Implement Luhn algorithm validation for credit card numbers. Current validation only checks length (16 chars), allowing invalid card numbers to pass validation.

Implement comprehensive test suite with 0% current coverage. All 6 functions are untested, including critical payment processing logic. Add tests for: processPremiumPayment success/failure paths, validatePaymentDetails edge cases, pricing calculations, database operations, feature access control, and integration flows.

Remove or sanitize sensitive data from error logging. console.error() at line 70 may log full error objects containing payment data or system details. Implement structured logging with data sanitization.
Add try-catch blocks around all JSON.parse() calls in hasFeatureAccess (line 75) and getUserSubscription (line 82). Corrupted database data could cause uncaught exceptions and application crashes.

Fix expiry date validation logic to handle century boundaries correctly and account for month-end dates. Current Y2K-style parsing (2000 + year) fails for future years and doesn't properly validate end-of-month expiration.

Add comprehensive input validation for all public function parameters: validate userId (not null/empty), validate payment.amount (positive, within reasonable bounds), add null/undefined checks for all payment fields.
Extract hard-coded pricing values and tax rates to a centralized configuration object. This allows easy pricing updates without code changes and enables testing with different pricing scenarios.
Implement Repository pattern to centralize database access. Extract queries from scattered functions into a dedicated data access layer for better maintainability, testability, and monitoring.
Improve error handling to distinguish between different failure types (database error, network error, validation error) instead of generic error handling that returns false for all cases.

Extract validation functions (isCardNumberValid, isCVVValid, isExpiryDateValid) from validatePaymentDetails to improve testability and enable reuse. Extract feature mapping and expiry date calculation from upgradeUserSubscription.
